blocks.text: A 42-year-old man killed while riding a roller-coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia was thrown from his seat and struck other patrons before landing below the ride, police said Tuesday.
Visitors to the Atlanta-area park watched in horror as he fell out of the coaster Monday, prompting Six Flags to temporarily close nine similar roller-coasters countrywide.
Investigators and park officials have not said how he ended up coming out of his seat.
"It was horrific to watch," said Summer Bates, who was at the park with her husband and three children. "One thing I think that will stick with us is the sound of his body coming down."

Bates said she and her family rode the Goliath roller-coaster earlier in the day. The park's tallest coaster, which towers over its entrance at 61 metres, has lap bar restraints that pull down over the riders' legs and waist. There are no seat belts.

"My older two children rode on the cart ahead of us," she said. "I noticed they kept trying to push theirs down tighter. I assured them that they were OK. But once my husband, youngest child and I loaded our cart and headed up the incline, I quickly understood why my older two were messing with theirs. It just didn't feel secure and tight."

The man who died was 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, according to Cobb County police. Officials have not released any other information about those who were injured when they were struck by the man.
Kariem worked as the information technology manager at a public charter school in Atlanta and before that was the school's technology teacher, according to an online resume.
Witness describes seeing man come out of his seat
Logan Conner said he was on the Goliath with his fiancée when he saw the man come out of his seat.
"The man started levitating in the air sideways," he told NBC. "We made direct eye contact with him."
WATCH | 1 dead, several injured in U.S. roller-coaster incident:
Britny Landry had been on the ride earlier Monday and was waiting in line to go again. She could see part of the Goliath track.
"We just look, and I just see somebody fly out," she told KTVU-TV. She said she wasn't sure if that's what she saw at first. "Maybe somebody had a bag or something."
Investigators say they spoke with park visitors and employees who saw what happened in the incident Monday at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, about 24 kilometres northwest of Atlanta.
Coasters closed in Canada and U.S.

Nine roller-coasters at six North American parks that are similar to the coaster in Georgia were closed "out of an abundance of caution," according to a Six Flags Entertainment Corporation spokesperson, who said staff members and local authorities responded immediately and the park is co-operating with the investigation.
"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said, adding that the company is providing support to guests and staff who were impacted.

CBC News has confirmed that the list of nine rides includes the Behemoth and Leviathan at Canada's Wonderland, north of Toronto. A park spokesperson said it did not have a timeline for when the rides might be available again.
Canada's Wonderland is open to the public for 12 more Halloween-themed evenings and weekends until it closes for the winter.

Montreal's La Ronde amusement park said it was temporarily shutting down its Goliath roller-coaster until an update is received from the manufacturer of the ride. La Ronde was a Six Flags property until this spring, when the park's purchase by EPR Properties was finalized.
Authorities and Six Flags did not identify the roller-coaster at the Georgia location. However, local TV stations showed video of passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster.

The roller-coaster, which was opened in 2006, reaches top speeds of about 113 km/h and heights of 61 metres, the park's website reports. During about 3½ minutes, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills," according to the website.

"I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners, said in a statement. She added that next of kin have been notified.
The amusement park is a major part of the county's tourism and brings in visitors from across the southeast, Cupid said.
"We are all grappling with how something so devastating could happen at a place that has given generations of families such happy memories," she said.

Georgia's Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner, which oversees ride inspections, is "conducting an in‑depth and comprehensive review," said Garrison Bennett, a spokesperson. The park was already scheduled to be closed Tuesday.

This death would be at least the seventh at the Georgia park, including one in 2006 in which a man had a likely heart attack on the Goliath coaster, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents.

It also comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain, in Southern California, announced that it is retiring its famous X2 roller-coaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride. The park had settled one wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022.

Last year, a 32-year-old man died after riding a high-speed roller-coaster at the Universal Epic Universe theme park in Florida. He died from blunt impact injuries, and his death was ruled accidental.

post.description:
Browse a section or region, optionally within a date range (for example everything CBC Edmonton published last week). Category slugs come from a search hit's category_slugs, from lookup_region's leaf_slug, or from the slug in a cbc.ca section URL (/news/canada/edmonton -> edmonton).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.0005 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category_slugs.description: CBC category slugs, for example ["edmonton"] or ["politics"]. Items in any of them are listed.

from.description: Earliest publish date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive from 00:00 UTC. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

page.description:
1-based page. Pass the `next_cursor` of the previous call to continue.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 1.

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 60; default 20.

sort.description:
Newest first by publish time (default) or by last-update time.

Provider reference: allowed values ["published", "updated"]; default "published".

to.description: Latest publish date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

types.description: Content types to include. Defaults to stories only.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Newest CBC items in one or more categories (sections or regions such as `edmonton`, `calgary`, `politics`, `world`) through CBC's aggregate_api `items` listing, optionally limited to a publish-date window (`from` / `to`, UTC calendar days, inclusive) and to content types (story, video). Sorted newest first by publish or last-update time; `page_size` up to 60. The API drops an unknown slug silently and would answer the whole site, so the function checks the API's `x-items-filters` echo: a slug CBC does not know is `not_found`, and every returned row is verified to carry a requested category. Rows are metadata only (title, deck, URL, publish and update instants, categories, media flags); use `get_article` for the text.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `items` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `categories` | object[] |  |
| `contains_audio` | boolean |  |
| `contains_photogallery` | boolean |  |
| `contains_video` | boolean |  |
| `deck` | string | Sub-headline. |
| `description` | string |  |
| `flag` | string | Editorial flag such as `Breaking`, `Updated`, `Analysis`; null when none. |
| `id` | number | Numeric id (the part after the dot of source_id). |
| `image_url` | string |  |
| `media_duration_s` | number | Media length in seconds for video/audio items. |
| `published_at` | string | RFC 3339 UTC. |
| `published_at_ms` | number |  |
| `show` | string | Programme name for broadcast items. |
| `source_id` | string |  |
| `title` | string |  |
| `type` | string |  |
| `updated_at` | string |  |
| `updated_at_ms` | number |  |
| `url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Resolve a Canadian place name to CBC's location taxonomy through GraphQL `searchCanadianCities`: label (`Edmonton, AB`), taxonomy path (`The Americas/North America/Canada/Alberta/Edmonton`), slug path, coordinates and the taxonomy leaf id. `leaf_slug` is the last segment of the slug path; for CBC's regional sections it is the category slug `list_articles` accepts (`edmonton`, `calgary`, `toronto`). An unknown name is an empty list, not an error.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `cities` as the primary payload key.

post.description:
Find CBC stories by keyword, optionally within a section, then call get_article with a hit's source_id for the full text. For a region or section within a date range use list_articles instead.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.0005 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

media.description:
`video` restricts hits to video content.

Provider reference: allowed values ["all", "video"]; default "all".

page.description:
1-based page of 10 hits. Pass the `next_cursor` of the previous call to continue.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 1.

section.description:
Site section as offered by the search page. `all` (default) searches every section.

Provider reference: allowed values ["all", "news", "sports", "radio", "music", "arts", "comedy", "books", "life"]; default "all".

sort.description:
`relevance` (default) or `newest` (the search page's Most recent).

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "newest"]; default "relevance".

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Keyword search across cbc.ca through the site's own GraphQL `allSearchItems` field, the backend of https://www.cbc.ca/search. Optional section filter (news, sports, radio, music, arts, comedy, books, life), sort by relevance or newest, and a video-only media filter. Fixed pages of 10 hits; `total_count` is the index's total for the query. Each hit carries CBC's dotted `source_id` (the key for `get_article`), title, description, canonical URL, content type, publish and last-updated instants (RFC 3339 UTC and epoch ms), bylines, category slugs and the tracking region (for example `edmonton`). The search index has no date-range argument: use `list_articles` for section or region plus date range.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authors` | string[] | Byline names as the search index stores them (may include `CBC News`). |
| `category_names` | string[] | Category paths (`News/Canada/Edmonton`); null when the index has no categories for the hit yet. |
| `category_slugs` | string[] | Category slugs (`edmonton`), usable as list_articles category_slugs; null when absent in the index. |
| `content_area` | string |  |
| `content_type` | string | CBC content type: story, video, audio, ... |
| `description` | string |  |
| `image_url` | string |  |
| `published_at` | string | Original publish instant, RFC 3339 UTC. |
| `published_at_ms` | number |  |
| `region` | string | CBC tracking subsection2: the regional slug (`edmonton`, `calgary`) when the hit belongs to a region. |
| `source_id` | string | CBC's dotted content id (`9.7378332`, legacy `1.633085`); the input of get_article. |
| `subsection` | string | CBC tracking subsection1 (`regions`, `politics`, ...). |
| `title` | string |  |
| `updated_at` | string | Last-updated instant, RFC 3339 UTC; equals published_at when never updated. |
| `updated_at_ms` | number |  |
| `url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

results.description: The Edmonton Chamber of Commerce says the next city budget should be fiscally responsible and focused on core services while also investing in initiatives that will grow the economy.
results.title: Basic repairs, downtown investment on Edmonton business group's budget wish list

results.description: Councillors narrowly approved a motion to break down how much it would cost to launch a fare gate pilot project at one downtown LRT station. The viability of the project will be determined during budget deliberations in November.
results.title: Edmonton city council to vote on fare gate pilot project in November

results.description: Edmonton-based Studio Reset was founded by developers with years of experience working at studios like Electronic Arts-owned Bioware. As companies with billion-dollar budgets become more risk averse chasing the next big hit, it could be the best way for developers to flex their creative muscles.
results.title: Edmonton-based indie game studio latest to take blockbuster-making skills and get 'pretty risky'

results.description: The Edmonton Regional Airports Authority is lobbying federal and provincial government officials to discuss defence and economic development, amid Ottawa’s renewed commitment to the armed forces. Experts say there’s an opportunity for the Edmonton airport to grow its business.
results.title: Edmonton airport trying to align with national defence strategy, lobbying records show

results.description: Edmonton’s under-construction Lewis Farms Recreation Centre has a new price tag — and the project could cost almost $32 million more than the city expected.
results.title: Edmonton's Lewis Farms rec centre could cost nearly $32M more than original estimate

results.description: Mayor Andrew Knack campaigned on getting more everyday people involved in shaping the city’s priorities for the next four-year budget. That process is now underway, with a survey open until May 1, and in-person engagement sessions scheduled next month.
results.title: ‘Please get involved’: Edmonton mayor wants to know your budget priorities

results.description: A report heading to city council on Wednesday says the Lewis Farms project is facing higher inflation than predicted. City staff recommend council use an undisclosed amount from the capital budget to pay for the difference.
results.title: Edmonton Lewis Farms Recreation Centre over budget, despite being significantly scaled back

results.description: Mayor Andrew Knack says while he’s grateful the provincial government has reinstated municipal grants and is investing in Edmonton’s downtown, its latest budget doesn’t meet the mark for the city’s infrastructure needs.
results.title: Edmonton mayor says province’s ‘status quo’ 2026 budget leaves infrastructure gaps

results.description: The province has signalled significant budget challenges lie ahead. Mayor Andrew Knack said he’s aware of that, but has eyes on Edmonton’s $1.5-billion renewal deficit.
